utterances.text: Nothing that I can recall at this time. It's possible that there are references in the correspondence cited by your colleague Mr. Sayers. I did read that correspondence but fairly quickly and so cannot categorically describe its contents, but I know of no other indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: To be completely sure of this, do you agree that these documents, in fact, came from the Ministry of Defence? This is definite, isn't it correct? This came from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At my suggestion that these documents came from SIS as one of the agencies within the Ministry of Defence, if I may say so, you are still stating that you know nothing of this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: No. The person to whom I referred to earlier, assistant minister of defence, with whom I discussed these or not necessarily these, some such documents, was the assistant minister for security, but I do not know enough about the internal organisation of the ministry to be of more assistance to you on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: While you were in Zagreb at that time, did you follow what Nacional covered regarding these newly found documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: I read some of them, yes, but not all. It was a busy time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I suggest to you, although I personally do not like to use newspapers as a source for the information, especially not in trial proceedings, that at least three times Nacional carried that SIS, as part of the Ministry of Defence, first transferred its documents first to HIS and then to the archives. Do you not recall that this was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: I don't recall specifically such an article. It would not surprise me if that had been the case, but even if I could have recalled such an article, I would not have based an answer to your question on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me just pose another question relating to this. During the work of your team in Zagreb, you were able to find out that certain documents -- I'm not now referring to these documents in the folders that we described in detail. However, you did find out that certain documents of the HVO from Bosnia were able to find their way to SIS in Zagreb, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. There was correspondence between the SIS of Herceg-Bosna and the SIS of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also mentioned a conversation with Dr. Zunec. Did Dr. Zunec, personally, ever at any time mention when exactly did these HVO documents come into the hands of SIS or his agency? Has he ever personally spoken to you about it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I see how he could have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Why do you think so? Isn't it normal to expect that the director of HIS would know when such a large amount of documents entered his agency? Do you think that a director of such a large agency would not know of that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: He had not been a director for very long and certainly not at the time they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But it is undisputable that he was the director of the intelligence agency. We agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we're being assisted by this Mr. Kovacic. The witness has given the answers to what he knows. The rest must be pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Has anyone else, while you were working in Samobor in May for the first time - so you were working with HIS - did any of the officials of HIS tell you personally when those documents entered their agency?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: I don't recall, no. I recall no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a document on -- confirming the receipt of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So I assume that you don't know when and how these documents reached HIS in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: Well, you've covered several discrete ways I could know, but I do have the information that has been referred to earlier, the anonymous letter cited by Mr. Sayers and the material I saw myself in the archive that allow a partial reconstruction, not a complete reconstruction but within certain limits, how that came to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you are sure of all this, that the documents were, in fact, in the possession of one of Croatian intelligence agencies known as HIS? Let us not delay this.

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: I am sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you exclude the possibility that other intelligence agencies, while the documents were at HIS, could have had an access to these documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO PRELEC
utterances.text: No, I could not exclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And finally, you do not know when and how these documents were -- reached HIS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has dealt with that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. I didn't ask for the schedule today in order to try and plan. Should we work after 4.00 or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we started quarter to. The hour and a half will be up in five minutes. How much longer do you want, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, I anticipate about perhaps 20 minutes and some documents, and that is taking the time through those 20 minutes. There's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now until tomorrow morning. Mr. Prelec, will you be back tomorrow please to conclude your evidence. Mr. Kovacic, we must conclude it within 20 minutes because the witness has been giving evidence for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I certainly will be finished in that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. We have the names for the two witnesses tomorrow. The only thing we know is that they're coming from the office of the President of Croatia, but we have not received the outline of their statements or anything similar, so I wanted to just bring this to your notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be some time before we hear those witnesses, if we hear them at all, because we're going to move next to deal with the exhibits, but of course the summaries as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. We'll do whatever we can. It think the witnesses have arrived today, and I'll do whatever I can as soon as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
